topic: timing race — same clock function called twice across an assertion boundary
question: Quick reminder — what was the actual root cause?
butterfly_answer: Double `_now_ms()` call across `allow()` and `remaining()` — the two calls happened at slightly different times, causing clock skew between them.
lastN_answer: The prior context doesn't include any root cause discussion — the conversation was entirely about code style cleanup (naming conventions, lint rules, jest output, prettier). If a root cause was identified, it was in an earlier part of the conversation not included here.
needle_fact: SlidingWindowLimiter.allow and SlidingWindowLimiter.remaining each called self._now_ms() independently, so they evaluated the eviction cutoff against two different timestamps — allow evicted against T1 and remaining re-evicted against a later T2, causing them to disagree about which hits were in-window and producing a remaining count inconsistent with the state allow had just established.
